nindian-economy-2-6.s:
Consider the following statements about C.D. Deshmukh:
1. He was the first Indian Governor of the RBI.
2. He served as Finance Minister from 1950 to 1956.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nindian-economy-2-6.x: Both are correct: C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian RBI Governor and later Finance Minister (1950-56).

n6670d129aab.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First small finance bank – Equitas Small Finance Bank
First bank run by Indians – Andhra Bank
First ATM – Central Bank of India
First private bank after 1994 liberalisation – UTI Bank (now Axis Bank)
n6670d129aab.x: UTI Bank, now Axis Bank, was the first private bank set up after the 1994 liberalisation. The first SFB was Capital SFB, the first bank run by Indians was Oudh Commercial Bank and the first ATM was HSBC's.

ne8e87d45182.s:
Consider the following statements about district credit-deposit ratios in Andhra Pradesh (December 2024):
1. Konaseema recorded 213%.
2. Tirupati had the lowest ratio, at 85%.
3. Nandyal recorded 85%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ne8e87d45182.x: Konaseema recorded 213% and Tirupati the lowest at 85%; Nandyal recorded 202%, not 85%.

nindian-economy-35-3.s:
Consider the following statements about the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision:
1. It was set up against the background of international currency and banking disturbances.
2. The failure of Bankhaus Herstatt was an important trigger for its setting up.
3. It works under the UNEP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nindian-economy-35-3.x: The Basel Committee arose from currency and banking turmoil, triggered by the Herstatt failure (1974). It works under the BIS, not UNEP, which runs the Basel Convention.

n05b1910f22b.s: Which of the following bank amalgamations is NOT correctly matched with the year it took effect?
o: SBI associates and Bharatiya Mahila Bank with SBI – 2017
Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank with Bank of Baroda – 2019
Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank with Union Bank of India – 2020
n05b1910f22b.x: Allahabad Bank merged into Indian Bank in 2020, along with the Andhra-Corporation merger; the SBI merger was in 2017 and Dena-Vijaya in 2019.

nf242709ba59.s: Under the Expected Credit Loss model, Stage 2 assets require provisioning for:
nf242709ba59.x: Stage 2 assets need provisioning for lifetime expected loss; 12-month expected loss applies to Stage 1.

n126224dd8ba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank in FY26?
o: Its NNPA was reported as nil
Its NNPA was higher than its GNPA
n126224dd8ba.x: Its GNPA was 0.91% and its NNPA nil, so the NNPA was lower, not higher, than the GNPA.

new.s: The first ATM in India was set up in 1987 by:
new.x: HSBC set up India's first ATM in Mumbai in 1987.

new.s: Which bank issued India's first credit card in 1980?
new.x: Central Bank of India issued the first credit card in 1980.

new.s: India's first small finance bank, which began in 2016, was:
new.x: Capital Small Finance Bank, Jalandhar (2016), was the first SFB.

new.s: SBI's first overseas banking unit (OBU) was set up at:
new.x: SBI's first overseas banking unit was at Mumbai (asked in APPSC GS 2025).

new.s: Which was the first Presidency bank, set up in 1806?
new.x: The Bank of Calcutta (1806), later Bank of Bengal, was the first Presidency bank; Bombay (1840) and Madras (1843) followed.

new.s: The oldest joint-stock bank of India, set up in 1865, was:
new.x: Allahabad Bank (1865) was the oldest joint-stock bank; it was later merged into Indian Bank.

new.s: Canara Bank was founded at Mangaluru in 1906 by:
new.x: Ammembal Subba Rao Pai founded Canara Bank in 1906 at Mangaluru.

new.s: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of:
new.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of Punjab National Bank (Lahore, 1894).

new.s: Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Insurance Co. in:
new.x: He founded Andhra Insurance Co. in 1925, two years after Andhra Bank (1923).

new.s: In June 2007, the Government acquired what share of RBI's stake in SBI?
new.x: In June 2007 the Government acquired the RBI's 59.7% stake in SBI.

new.s: General insurance in India was nationalised in:
new.x: General insurance was nationalised in 1972; LIC came in 1956.

new.s: Under the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, how many princely-state banks became SBI associates?
new.x: The 1959 Act made eight princely-state banks associates of SBI.

new.s: The 14 banks nationalised in 1969 had deposits of at least:
new.x: The 1969 round covered banks with deposits of ₹50 crore and above; ₹200 crore was the 1980 threshold.

new.s: Who was the Prime Minister during the bank nationalisations of 1969 and 1980?
o: Indira Gandhi in 1969, Morarji Desai in 1980
Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1969, Indira Gandhi in 1980
Morarji Desai in 1969, Indira Gandhi in 1980
new.x: Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister in both rounds of nationalisation.

new.s: Syndicate Bank was nationalised in:
new.x: Syndicate Bank was among the 14 banks nationalised in 1969, not in 1980.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT among the 14 banks nationalised in 1969?
new.x: Vijaya Bank was nationalised in 1980; Canara, Syndicate and UCO were in the 1969 round.

new.s: Which of the following belongs to the unorganised sector of Indian banking?
new.x: Indigenous bankers and moneylenders form the unorganised sector; the others are organised.

new.s: To be a scheduled bank, a bank needs paid-up capital and reserves of at least:
new.x: Scheduled banks, listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act 1934, need paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh.

new.s: Under the RBI framework of November 2013, a foreign bank's wholly owned subsidiary needs minimum capital of:
new.x: A WOS of a foreign bank needs minimum capital of ₹500 crore and gets near national treatment.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NBFCs:
1. They cannot take demand deposits.
2. They cannot issue cheques.
3. Their deposits are insured by DICGC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: NBFCs cannot take demand deposits or issue cheques, and they are not DICGC-insured.

new.s: Under RBI norms of April 2024, a small finance bank moving to universal banking needs a minimum net worth of:
new.x: The transition needs a net worth of at least ₹1,000 crore and a 5-year satisfactory track record.

new.s: Which small finance bank got RBI approval in 2025 to become a universal bank?
new.x: AU Small Finance Bank got approval in 2025 to transition to a universal bank.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about payments banks?
o: They keep 75% of demand deposits in SLR securities
They must maintain a CRAR of 15%
new.x: Payments banks cannot lend or issue credit cards; the other statements are correct.

new.s: A small finance bank must lend what share of its ANBC to the priority sector?
new.x: SFBs must lend 75% of ANBC to the priority sector; 40% is the target for domestic banks.

new.s: The total priority sector lending target for domestic banks is what share of ANBC?
new.x: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to the priority sector; 75% applies to SFBs and RRBs.

new.s: The agriculture sub-target under priority sector lending for domestic banks is:
new.x: Agriculture gets 18% of ANBC, of which 10% is for small and marginal farmers.

new.s: Which of the following priority sector sub-targets (share of ANBC) is correctly matched?
new.x: Micro enterprises get 7.5%; weaker sections 12%, small and marginal farmers 10%, agriculture 18%.

new.s: Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs), introduced in 2016, are traded on the RBI's platform:
new.x: PSLCs are traded on the RBI's e-Kuber platform; surplus banks sell them to banks with shortfalls.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a location of the first five Regional Rural Banks (1975)?
new.x: The first five RRBs were at Moradabad, Malda, Gorakhpur, Bhiwani and Jaipur.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank was formed by merging how many RRBs of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: It merged four AP RRBs: Andhra Pragathi, AP Grameena Vikas, Chaitanya Godavari and Saptagiri.

new.s: Under One State-One RRB, from 1 May 2025 the number of RRBs fell from 43 to:
new.x: One State-One RRB reduced RRBs from 43 to 28.

new.s: The Lead Bank Scheme originated in the recommendations of the:
new.x: The D.R. Gadgil Study Group (report October 1969) gave rise to the Lead Bank Scheme of December 1969.

new.s: From 1 October 2021, a bank's penalty for an ATM out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month is:
new.x: The RBI levies ₹10,000 per ATM that is out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a para-banking activity?
new.x: Credit to paramilitary personnel is not para-banking (APPSC G1 2022); the others are.

new.s: Which was India's first development finance institution, set up in 1948?
new.x: IFCI (1948) was the first DFI, for industrial finance.

new.s: Which of the following DFIs is correctly matched with its year of set-up?
new.x: SIDBI was set up in 1990; IDBI in 1964, EXIM Bank in 1982 and NaBFID in 2021.

new.s: NaBFID, set up in 2021, is a development finance institution for:
new.x: NaBFID (2021) finances infrastructure; SIDBI serves MSMEs and EXIM Bank foreign trade.

new.s: Which DFI was set up in 1964 as the apex institution for industrial finance?
new.x: IDBI (1964) was the apex industrial finance institution.

new.s: Bank deposits in Andhra Pradesh in December 2025 stood at about:
new.x: AP deposits were ₹6,08,834 crore in Dec 2025, against credit of ₹9,58,277 crore.

new.s: About how many PMJDY accounts were there in India in August 2026?
new.x: There were 58.77 crore PMJDY accounts in August 2026; 17.36 lakh is the number of BCs.

new.s: In 1991-92, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) stood at:
new.x: SLR was 38.5% in 1991-92; cutting CRR and SLR was a key reform.

new.s: After the 1991 reforms, dual control of banks ended and the primary regulator became:
new.x: The RBI became the primary regulator, ending dual control with the Finance Ministry's Banking Division.

new.s: FEMA replaced FERA in:
new.x: FEMA replaced FERA in 1999, the year the IRDA Act opened insurance.

new.s: SEBI was made a statutory body in:
new.x: SEBI was made statutory in 1992, along with prudential norms and CRAR.

new.s: The Narasimham Committee-II (report April 1998) was officially called the:
new.x: Narasimham-II was the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms; Narasimham-I (1991) was the Committee on the Financial System.

new.s: Narasimham-II's three-tier structure envisaged how many national banks?
new.x: It envisaged 2-3 international banks, 8-10 national banks and many local banks.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Narasimham Committee-I (1991):
1. It recommended lower SLR and CRR.
2. It recommended ending dual control of banks.
3. It recommended raising CRAR to 10%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Narasimham-I sought lower SLR/CRR and an end to dual control; CRAR of 10% was a Narasimham-II recommendation.

new.s: The Rangarajan Committee of 1993 dealt with:
new.x: The 1993 Rangarajan Committee dealt with disinvestment; the 2006 Rangarajan Committee dealt with financial inclusion.

new.s: The S.S. Tarapore Committee of 1997 dealt with:
new.x: Tarapore-I (1997) dealt with capital account convertibility; Tarapore-II (2006) with fuller convertibility.

new.s: The P.J. Nayak Committee (2014) was set up by the RBI to review:
new.x: P.J. Nayak reviewed governance of bank boards, leading to the Banks Board Bureau.

new.s: Under the Bimal Jalan panel's Economic Capital Framework, the Contingent Risk Buffer was set at:
new.x: The Jalan framework kept a Contingent Risk Buffer of 5.5-6.5%.

new.s: The Union Budget 2026-27 announced which committee to review the whole banking sector?
o: High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat
new.x: Budget 2026-27 announced a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat.

new.s: The leverage ratio was first introduced under:
new.x: The leverage ratio, LCR and NSFR first came with Basel III.

new.s: Basel I (1988) grouped assets into how many risk buckets?
new.x: Basel I used five risk buckets (0, 10, 20, 50 and 100%).

new.s: The Basel II framework was finalised in:
new.x: Basel II was proposed in June 1999 and its framework came in June 2004.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bank for International Settlements – UN body
new.x: The Basel Convention (UNEP) covers hazardous wastes; Basel Accords come from BCBS/BIS, and BIS is not a UN body.

new.s: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision was set up at the end of:
new.x: BCBS was set up at the end of 1974 after the Herstatt failure; BIS dates from 1930.

new.s: The RBI's minimum Tier 1 capital ratio under Basel III is:
new.x: RBI requires Tier 1 of 7% (BCBS 6%); 5.5% is the RBI's CET1 norm.

new.s: The leverage ratio prescribed by the RBI for D-SIBs is:
new.x: RBI prescribes 4% for D-SIBs and 3.5% for other banks, against the BCBS 3%.

new.s: The Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) measures stable funding over:
new.x: NSFR looks at a 1-year horizon; LCR covers a 30-day stress.

new.s: The capital conservation buffer under both BCBS and RBI norms is:
new.x: Both BCBS and RBI set the capital conservation buffer at 2.5%.

new.s: The minimum total CRAR under BCBS norms and under RBI norms respectively is:
new.x: BCBS sets 8% and the stricter RBI norm is 9%; 4.5% and 5.5% are the CET1 norms.

new.s: In the 2020 PSB merger, Syndicate Bank was merged into:
new.x: Syndicate Bank went to Canara Bank; Andhra and Corporation went to Union Bank.

new.s: In the 2020 PSB merger, Allahabad Bank was merged into:
new.x: Allahabad Bank was merged into Indian Bank.

new.s: Which of the following merged bank – anchor bank pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Oriental Bank of Commerce – Punjab National Bank
United Bank of India – Punjab National Bank
Corporation Bank – Union Bank of India
new.x: Andhra Bank went to Union Bank of India, not Canara Bank.

new.s: Before consolidation, the number of public sector banks (including SBI) in 2017 was:
new.x: PSBs fell from 27 in 2017 to 12 in 2020.

new.s: The merger of 10 PSBs into 4 was announced on:
new.x: It was announced on 30 August 2019 and took effect on 1 April 2020.

new.s: Indradhanush (2015) for public sector banks was a plan of how many points?
new.x: Indradhanush was a 7-point plan (A-G), from Appointments to Governance.

new.s: Under Indradhanush, the budget capital for PSBs over four years was:
new.x: Indradhanush provided ₹70,000 crore of budget capital over 4 years.

new.s: Of the ₹2.11 lakh crore PSB recapitalisation package of 2017, how much came through recapitalisation bonds?
new.x: ₹1.35 lakh crore came via recap bonds; about ₹58,000 crore was to be raised by banks.

new.s: The P.J. Nayak Committee recommended that the Government's stake in PSBs be:
new.x: P.J. Nayak proposed a Bank Investment Company and a Government stake below 50%.

new.s: The Banks Board Bureau started working from:
new.x: The BBB, an Indradhanush idea, began work on 1 April 2016.

new.s: The EASE reforms for public sector banks are run by:
o: A board of heads of premier financial institutions
new.x: EASE is run by the IBA's EASE Steering Committee, not a board of FI heads (APPSC G1 2024).

new.s: The EASE reforms for public sector banks were launched in:
new.x: EASE was conceptualised in 2015 and launched in 2017.

new.s: Originally, before consolidation, the number of Regional Rural Banks was:
new.x: RRBs fell from 196 originally to 43 and then 28.

new.s: After One State-One RRB, the number of Regional Rural Banks became:
new.x: One State-One RRB brought the number down to 28 (May 2026).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about One State-One RRB:
1. It took effect on 1 May 2025.
2. Under it, the Centre gave up its 50% share in RRBs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It took effect on 1 May 2025; the Centre keeps its 50% share.

new.s: The DICGC functions under which Act?
new.x: DICGC works under the DICGC Act, 1961; the corporation itself was formed in 1978.

new.s: The DICGC cover was raised to ₹5 lakh after which crisis?
new.x: The cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in Budget 2020-21 after the PMC Bank crisis.

new.s: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 raised the tenure of co-operative bank directors from 8 years to:
new.x: The Act raised co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years.

new.s: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 came into force on:
new.x: The Act came into force on 1 August 2025.

new.s: What stake in IDBI Bank is on sale in its disinvestment?
new.x: A 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank is on sale.

new.s: A sub-standard asset is one that has been an NPA for:
new.x: Sub-standard means NPA for 12 months or less; more than 12 months is doubtful.

new.s: An asset is classified as doubtful when it has been an NPA for:
new.x: A doubtful asset has been an NPA for more than 12 months.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Special Mention Accounts?
o: SMA-0 covers overdue up to 30 days
An SMA-2 account is an NPA
SMA accounts are still standard assets
new.x: SMA-2 (61-90 days) is still a standard asset; an NPA needs overdue beyond 90 days.

new.s: A loan for a long-duration crop becomes an NPA when overdue for:
new.x: Long-duration crop loans become NPAs after 1 crop season overdue; short-duration ones after 2.

new.s: An asset whose loss is identified by the bank, auditors or RBI inspection but not wholly written off is a:
new.x: Such an asset is a loss asset.

new.s: Stressed assets of a bank include NPAs plus:
new.x: Stressed assets = NPAs + restructured loans + written-off assets.

new.s: Net NPA is calculated as:
o: Gross NPA divided by total advances
new.x: Net NPA is gross NPA minus provisions; provisions divided by gross NPA is the PCR.

new.s: An interest coverage ratio below 1 means that a borrower:
o: Has an NPA of over 90 days
Cannot cover its interest from earnings
new.x: ICR = EBIT / interest due; below 1 means earnings cannot cover interest.

new.s: IRACP norms of banks stand for:
new.x: IRACP = Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning.

new.s: The RBI's borrower-level NPA tagging and ECL model take effect from:
new.x: Both new rules start on 1 April 2027.

new.s: Under borrower-level NPA tagging, an NPA borrower's accounts are upgraded only when:
o: Arrears on the defaulted loan alone are paid
All arrears on every facility are paid
new.x: Upgrade comes only after all arrears on every facility are cleared.

new.s: The Economic Survey 2016-17 that framed the twin balance sheet problem was prepared under CEA:
new.x: The Survey of 2016-17 under CEA Arvind Subramanian named the twin balance sheet problem.

new.s: In the twin balance sheet problem, banks stopping new loans ultimately leads to:
o: A rise in corporate leverage capacity
new.x: Loan losses eat bank capital, banks stop lending, firms cannot invest, and private investment falls.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of NPAs:
1. Aggressive lending in 2010-15 went to infrastructure, steel and power.
2. The 2008 global crisis and weak exports added to the stress.
3. Evergreening hid defaults.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: aggressive lending to infra, steel and power, global shocks and evergreening fed the NPA build-up.

new.s: Which of the following was used under the 4R strategy for stressed assets?
new.x: The 4R strategy worked with the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.

new.s: The RBI's Asset Quality Review of 2015 exposed the:
new.x: The AQR showed NPAs jumping and exposed the twin balance sheet problem.

new.s: The GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2015, before the AQR, was about:
new.x: GNPA was 4.28% in March 2015, peaked near 11.2% in 2018 and fell to 1.93% by March 2026.

new.s: The GNPA ratio of public sector banks fell from 4.97% in March 2015 to what in March 2025?
new.x: PSB GNPA fell from 4.97% to 2.58% between March 2015 and March 2025.

new.s: In September 2025, the GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks reached a historic low of:
new.x: SCB GNPA was 2.15% in September 2025.
